Subject: Skylark MSA - proposed IP carveouts + output usage

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and Order Form (Skylark_MSA_Redlines.pdf). Two areas we want to call out up front so you can route to the right teams:

1) Output ownership / productization: Skylark needs explicit rights to use, reproduce, and commercialize model outputs derived from our data in our internal products and downstream SaaS offerings. We are asking for an assignment or a non-exclusive, perpetual license in the Order Form Exhibit that covers generated content.

2) Training / retraining: We cannot permit Redwood to use our customer-provided content to retrain models that could be made available to other customers without an opt-in consent. We expect a carveout in the Feedback/Training clause and clear operational controls (isolation, opt-in flows, audit evidence).

Additionally, the redlines include language about feedback license scope and a request for telemetry/evidence that training did not occur (audit log snapshots). Please confirm who at Redwood will be handling these items so we can correlate with our procurement/legal review.

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement and, ideally, proposed alternative language we can review.

Best,
Evan Cole
Senior Counsel – Skylark Systems

Subject: Skylark - proposed contract language (working draft)

Team —

I pulled together a concise proposal to use as a starting point when we reply to Skylark. Key tradeoffs called out inline. See below; I’ll drop a tidy redline_summary.docx to the Drive after we align.

1) Output ownership (Order Form Exhibit A) — Path A (preferred for large enterprise):
"Customer shall own Customer Outputs produced solely from Customer-provided prompts, data, and templates. Redwood hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to such Customer Outputs, subject to Customer’s compliance with the Agreement."
Tradeoff: Assignment gives Skylark the cleanest productization story but may set expectations for downstream model-building. Limit assignment to outputs (not model weights or derived datasets. )

Path B (alternate — license):
"Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and commercialize Customer Outputs produced from Customer-provided inputs for Customer’s internal and commercial products."
Tradeoff: License preserves Redwood’s ability to continue model development; assignment is more customer-friendly.

2) Training / Feedback (MSA §X) — draft carveout: 
"Redwood will not use Customer Content, Customer Outputs, or aggregated logs that are reasonably attributable to Customer for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, or improving any models made available to third parties, except with Customer’s prior written consent. For clarity, operational telemetry and ephemeral logs used for system debugging are excluded from this restriction if anonymized and not used to update production models. Upon Customer’s request, Redwood will provide a quarterly attestation describing whether training on Customer-derived materials occurred during the prior quarter and will produce relevant audit log excerpts to support the attestation."

Tradeoff: Provides contractual protection and a lightweight audit path without committing to continuous disclosure of internal training manifests. If Skylark needs stronger guarantees (no retention for debug logs), we can add data retention / deletion windows.

3) Evidence & Ops: Provide a one-page appendix describing how the opt-out is enforced (tagging customer inputs, separated queues, KV caching rules, and training manifest filters).

Rishi — can you vet the legal correctness / add any compliance language? Laura — once Rishi gives signoff we should give Evan both Path A and Path B and ask Skylark which they prefer. Recommend adding a proposal for a short migration window if they request assignment.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Evan —

Thanks for sending the redlines. We reviewed internally and attached a short summary with two proposal paths and operational notes (redline_summary.docx, also uploaded to the Drive). High-level response:

- Output rights: we can offer either an assignment of Customer Outputs limited to content produced solely from Customer-provided inputs (Order Form Exhibit A) or, alternatively, a perpetual non-exclusive license for commercial use. I’ve flagged Path A as enterprise-standard when customers want a clean commercialization handoff; Path B is an option if you prefer to limit scope.

- Training/Feedback: proposed MSA language (below) prevents Redwood from using Customer Content or Customer Outputs for retraining without prior written consent and commits us to a quarterly attestation plus supporting audit excerpts.

Proposed MSA clause (draft):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content, Customer Outputs, or logs attributable to Customer for the purpose of training, fine‑tuning, or improving models made available to third parties, except with Customer’s prior written consent. Operational debug logs may be retained for up to 30 days for support purposes if anonymized; such logs will not be included in model training datasets. Upon request, Redwood will provide a quarterly attestation and supporting audit log excerpts evidencing compliance with this clause."

Next steps: please let us know which output path you prefer (Assignment vs Perpetual License) and whether the quarterly attestation + 30‑day debug log retention window meets your evidentiary needs. If Skylark needs a stronger commitment (e.g., documented deletion within 7 days or on-prem telemetry push), we can put that into the Order Form as a negotiated SLA.

I’ve copied Rishi and Laura for any contractual clarifications. If you’re available, Ben and I can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the options.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
